author: pgaudet
body: Hi @DaiqingChen @Matrisome Looking at Figure 1 in the paper cited here, it seems like the TGF beta complex is in the ECM in an inactive state. Therefore, we should not assert that TGF beta complex is part of the ECM (even though it *can* be part of the ECM, but we only capture the active state). This information would be captured as an annotation, something along the lines of 'fibronectin' enables 'sequestering activity' of TGF beta. Am I interpreting the figure correctly? Thanks, Pascale

Logical quibble: how do we annotate activation and function if we can't have an inactive state to start from?

author: pgaudet
body: Well the CC should be the location where the protein is active.

author: Matrisome
body: @deustp01 @pgaudet In the case of the TGF beta complex, it is first secreted as inactive in the interstitial ECM, but this is also where it gets activated, so no issue there.

author: pgaudet
body: Actually, this is very interesting: it gets activated in the ECM, but it seems to be active at the plasma membrane, isn't it ?

author: Matrisome
body: @pgaudet It is a question of perspective! The activation is the result of the binding of integrins to the LTBP TGFbeta associates with. This binding induces a change in the conformation of the complex and TGFbeta becomes accessible to its own cell surface receptors (TGFBR). TGFbeta remains in the ECM, but it gets in close proximity with the plasma membrane where its receptor (TGFBR) is to initiate its signaling functions. Does that make sense?

author: Matrisome
body: @pgaudet can you confirm that this annotation request has been completed? If so, we can move to "Done"

author: pgaudet
body:
Hi @Matrisome 
I confirmed with @thomaspd - this doesn't fit the GO guidelines: 
Being *activated* in a location is not the same as being active there. 

The ligand is active in the extracellular space (like all secreted ligands are represented in GO) -- not ~plasma membrane~. So we cannot add these relations.
